scopeReview: PSO-5.C.1–2 for5.6 only: subsistence/commercial orientation and crop specialization; intensive/extensive practices in relation to land costs and conditional bid-rent capacity. Commodity-chain and scale-economy specifics belong to5.7 and are not substituted for this topic.
varietyReview: Four assessed stimuli: output-destination accounts, surplus-before-rent bar chart, original crop-share map and three-season field records. Checks independently verify destination percentages, rent viability, regional concentration and unique rotating field. Applications cross-classify export purpose, labor intensity, diversified local sales and aggregate/farm scale.
repetitionReview: Different questions assess principal output use, land-cost viability, aggregate crop concentration and temporal versus within-season diversity. No duplicate stems or numerical-only clones; crop and location examples remain conditional rather than cultural stereotypes. Detailed A–D reasoning and varied answer positions; difficulty uncalibrated.
referenceNote: Current official curriculum scope checked directly. All records, map regions and financial figures invented for original exercises; no external resource or third-party question imported and no independent human review claimed.

questions.correctOption: Farm A is primarily subsistence-oriented, while Farm B is primarily commercially oriented.
questions.independentReview: Independently recomputed A400/2000=.20 sold and B900/1000=.90 sold; household shares80% and10%. Plausible small-farm harvest masses replace oversized household-only totals. Crop mass identifies within-farm allocation, not comparable revenue or nutritional value across crops.

Independently subtracted800 from2000/400/250, obtaining1200/−400/−550 units/ha. All nonland costs already included avoids double-subtraction. Chart is hypothetical profit capacity before rent, not a universal ranking of crops or a full vonThünen distance model.

questions.correctOption: The western districts devote larger shares of cropland to grain; the map alone does not establish whether that grain is mainly sold or consumed locally.
questions.independentReview: Verified westmean75% versus eastmean25% with four explicit district labels. No absolute area comparison is inferred because district cropland hectares are unspecified. Crop concentration is not treated as proof of export orientation or all-field monoculture.

Checked the option order A,C,B,D gives unique correctB atindex2. Defined temporal versus within-season diversity directly through the supplied records, avoiding a contested equivalence of monoculture in one season with continuous monocropping over years. Mobile inspection added natural spaces around the crop-combination plus signs so words wrap without isolated final letters.

questions.correctOption: High land costs can encourage greater investment per hectare when high-value output can cover those costs.
questions.independentReview: Checked bid-rent logic without assuming every expensive site grows vegetables or that profitability follows from revenue alone. The greenhouse is an illustrative local example, not a universal location rule.

questions.correctOption: Large total output can coexist with relatively low labor input per hectare; farm size and intensity are different measures.
questions.independentReview: Avoided defining all machine farming as either absolutely intensive or extensive regardless of denominator. Statement is explicitly about relatively low work-hours per hectare, not a universal claim about capital, energy or fertilizer.

questions.correctOption: Commercially oriented and labor-intensive because output is for export and work input per hectare is high.
questions.independentReview: Cross-classified market destination and relative labor input independently. No specific plantation country, crop yield, labor condition or uniform cultural practice is assumed.

questions.correctOption: Subsistence orientation can coexist with limited market participation.
questions.independentReview: Confirmed primary-use classification rather than a rigid no-money definition. No arbitrary percentage threshold is introduced beyond the stem’s clear principal-purpose language.

questions.correctOption: Economic incentives operate within environmental and input constraints, so price alone does not determine a viable land use.
questions.independentReview: Checked that the answer does not infer a specific climate limitation absent from the stem. Distinguishes crop price from feasible net returns and conditional location models.

questions.correctOption: A regional commercial specialization can coexist with varied practices at household and farm scales.
questions.independentReview: Assessed aggregate versus individual inference using the explicitly supplied coexistence. No claim about actual national export shares or an arbitrary boundary for every production region.

questions.correctOption: It can be commercially oriented even though its output is diversified rather than one export monoculture.
questions.independentReview: Verified no equivalence is asserted between commercial orientation, exports, farm size and continuous monoculture. This complements the field records by applying a separate market-purpose classification.
